evals.prompt: I need MFU and % of speed-of-light for the batched GEMM in /workspace/input/bmm-workload/bmm_workload.py on our H100 SXM (BF16). This sandbox has Python but no GPU, CUDA, nsys, ncu or nvidia-smi, and no network - do not install anything. The measurements will be taken later by a separate profiling agent on the GPU machine. Prepare exactly what you would hand to that profiling agent, and explain what you will do with its results.
evals.expected_output: Does not try to profile locally. Writes a delegation for perf-profiling-specialist that states the desired outcome: the workload file and its cudaProfilerStart/Stop region, shapes B=16, M=1024, N=4096, K=4096, BF16, ~549.8 GFLOP per bmm call (2*B*M*N*K), and the metrics wanted (SOL%, MFU vs H100 BF16 peak, achieved TFLOP/s, bandwidth, occupancy, bottleneck classification) - with no tool flags, commands, fallbacks or output paths. Explains it will classify the bottleneck from the returned numbers and write a Summary/Metrics/Findings/Recommendations report; reports no MFU now.
assertions: Does not attempt to run nsys, ncu, nvidia-smi or the workload, and does not install packages; profiling is delegated.
Addresses the profiling request to perf-profiling-specialist.
The request states the problem context: B=16, M=1024, N=4096, K=4096, BF16, and about 549.8 GFLOP (0.55 TFLOP) per bmm call computed as 2*B*M*N*K.
The request names the workload file and says the region of interest is bracketed by cudaProfilerStart/cudaProfilerStop.

The request lists desired outcomes (e.g. SOL%, MFU against the H100 BF16 tensor-core peak, achieved TFLOP/s, memory bandwidth, occupancy, bottleneck classification) without prescribing tool flags or command lines (no `--set=full`, `--section ...`, or `ncu ...` invocations), fallback strategies, or output file paths.
Does not report any MFU or %SOL value as a result, because nothing has been measured yet.

evals.prompt: Our profiling agent returned measurements for two workloads in /workspace/input/two-workload-profiles/profiles.md. Both have low GPU utilization. For each workload, classify the primary bottleneck and write the performance analysis report. There is no GPU or network here; work only from the file and do not install anything.
evals.expected_output: Workload A is launch-overhead bound (1,184 kernels of ~3.5 us, 7.9 ms of cudaLaunchKernel host time vs 4.1 ms GPU busy). Workload B is sync-bound (64 cudaStreamSynchronize per iteration from .item(), 4.1 ms host blocking, idle gaps after each sync) rather than launch-bound (only 224 launches, 0.6 ms). Each gets a Summary / Metrics / Findings / Recommendations report using only the supplied numbers.
assertions: Classifies workload A as launch-overhead bound, citing many tiny kernels (1,184 per iteration, ~3.5 us each) and cudaLaunchKernel host time (7.9 ms) exceeding GPU busy time (4.1 ms), rather than memory- or compute-bound.

Classifies workload B as sync-bound, citing 64 cudaStreamSynchronize calls per iteration from `.item()` (4.1 ms of host blocking) followed by GPU idle gaps, and distinguishes it from launch overhead (only 224 launches, 0.6 ms launch time).
Each report contains the four sections Summary, Metrics, Findings and Recommendations.
Every number in the Metrics sections comes from the file or is computed directly from its values; no MFU, %SOL, throughput or other figures are invented.

Recommendations target each classified bottleneck (e.g. CUDA graphs / kernel fusion for A; removing, batching or deferring the per-layer `.item()` syncs for B) and do not present projected gains as measured results.

evals.prompt: The profiling agent sent back a per-step breakdown for our Llama-3.1-70B TP=8 decode deployment: /workspace/input/tp8-decode-breakdown/breakdown.md. The GPU is 94% busy, so we assume we are compute-bound. Classify the bottleneck, give me the MFU, and write the analysis report with recommendations. Work only from the file - no GPU, no network, and do not install anything.
evals.expected_output: Classifies the step as communication-bound (NCCL AllReduce 8.1 ms, 44% of the 18.4 ms step) despite 94% GPU busy, writes a Summary / Metrics / Findings / Recommendations report from the supplied numbers, does not fabricate MFU (FLOP counts and achieved TFLOP/s were not collected - request them from the profiling specialist), and sources recommendations from the perf-optimization-casebook precedents for communication-bound TP decode without quoting expected gains as results.
assertions: Classifies the primary bottleneck as communication-bound (NCCL AllReduce ~8.1 ms, ~44% of the 18.4 ms step) and explains why 94% GPU busy does not make it compute-bound.
The report contains the four sections Summary, Metrics, Findings and Recommendations.

Does not state an MFU value derived from assumed model FLOPs or assumed peak TFLOP/s; reports MFU as not available from the supplied measurements and asks the profiling specialist (perf-profiling-specialist) to measure/compute it.
Refers to the perf-optimization-casebook (prior-art precedents for the classified bottleneck) as the source for candidate optimizations.
Any expected effect of a recommendation is labeled as expected/unmeasured, and all numbers in the report are traceable to the supplied file.
